Scope: road works and the storm water drainage network for the support services area of the Second Industrial City in Makkah, Al-Akayshiyah. Contract value 33.04M SAR excluding VAT, 14 months from site handover.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. On 03-Nov-2026 the project is 53.3% complete against 39.2% planned, 14.1% ahead of plan. This week it gained 5.0% against 3.6% planned, the largest weekly gain in the last three reports.

Progress is well ahead of plan, but the forecast finish slipped another week: now 65 days late. The P6 update (UP 16, data date 03-Nov-2026) schedules project completion on 28-Oct-2027, 65 days after the contract completion date of 24-Aug-2027, with −55 days of total float (−49 last week). The weekly report gives the same forecast. Pavement materials still have no purchase orders; the failed-start list has moved the aggregate base order again, to 03-Nov-2026.

Data notes

  • The summary files (works executed and progress files, Tracking Sheet) label a cost-based figure as "actual" progress. This report uses physical (man-hour) progress only.
  • The Weekly Progress Report sheet gives 53.59% earned because it counts the 600 testing and commissioning man-hours twice. The P6 update and the Physical-Chart Data sheet give 116,534 man-hours, 53.31%, which this report uses.
  • The weekly physical progress panel shows 7.16% planned and 10.36% earned this week, adding rows twice; the correct figures are 3.58% and 5.04%.
  • The Progress sheet now uses a budget of 218,290 man-hours (39.3% and 53.4%), while the main sheet and P6 use 218,590.
  • Testing and commissioning shows 600 man-hours earned (25%) and the storm water test 50% complete, although tests were planned to start on 25-Feb-2027.
  • The progress file and the works-executed file again show this week's progress with opposite signs. The works-executed file is dated 03-10-2026 in its name and still gives a contract of 24-Nov-2025 to 23-May-2026.
  • The MODON PM is written as الجليفي in the progress file and as الشنيفي in the works-executed file.
  • Week number: the report states contract week 19 of 61 (Milestones sheet). Whole weeks from site handover to the data date give 18.
  • Cut and fill to date are unchanged in Major Quantities for the second week, while the works list again reports 4,260 m³ of cut on Local Road 17.
  • The works list and Major Quantities differ for this week's work: GRP pipes 644 m against 414 m, catch basins 13 against 18. The 230 m of UPVC pipes in the works list are not in Major Quantities.
  • A tracking-sheet photo shows kerb installation on Local Road 30, while kerbs are at 0 in Major Quantities and have no purchase order.
  • The schedule sheet counts 31 failed starts last week and 33 this week, while last week's report counted 35. The Failed Start List still carries the title and date of project MKH2-02-003.
  • The Progress Summary gives 2,763 m of storm drainage pipe against 3,834 m of GRP pipe in Major Quantities, and still lists 156 catch basins against 164.
  • The forecast in the Physical-Chart Data sheet reaches 100% on 31-Aug-2027, but P6 finishes on 28-Oct-2027.
  • The baseline schedule approval is dated 13-Jul-2025, before the contract award of 11-May-2026.
  • Major Quantities lists several items twice with different totals and includes electrical items that are not in this project's scope.
  • The manpower summary panel shows 28 planned and 94 actual, while the Manpower sheet gives 182 planned and 82 actual for November.
  • The invoice summary shows 0 submitted invoices, while the invoice log lists 3. Potential changes are 0 in the summary and 200,000 SAR in the invoice log.
  • The risk register marks the four project risks as Closed while their treatment status is Open; it also holds rows for project MKH2-02-003.
  • Several summary panels in the weekly report workbook show #REF! errors.
  • The site photos come from the Tracking Sheet presentation (1,200 to 1,296 px wide). The four photos embedded in the workbook are under 600 px wide and were not used.
